# DealBreak Simulator — Complete Reference

> A free, browser-based real estate investing simulator game that teaches property deal analysis through interactive gameplay. No signup required. Also available as an iOS app.

## What Is DealBreak Simulator?

DealBreak Simulator is a turn-based educational game that teaches real estate underwriting — the analytical process investors use to evaluate whether a property deal will make or lose money. Players start with $100,000 in virtual cash and navigate a 52-month timeline, evaluating properties, building financial models, conducting due diligence, managing renovations and tenants, and experiencing realistic market events.

The game emphasizes the cause-and-effect relationships between assumptions (rent estimates, vacancy rates, repair budgets) and outcomes (cash flow, ROI, deal success or failure). Every playthrough is different thanks to randomized properties, market conditions, and events.

## Game Mechanics

### Property Analysis
Players browse randomized investment properties with realistic attributes: purchase price, estimated rent, square footage, condition (Excellent/Good/Fair/Fixer-Upper), property type (house/condo/apartment/townhouse/duplex/loft), and location. Each property has hidden issues that can be discovered through due diligence. Good/Turnkey/Excellent condition properties filter out cosmetic issues from issue pools.

### Pro Forma Financial Modeling
The core educational mechanic. Players build a pro forma spreadsheet for each deal:
- Gross rental income and vacancy assumptions
- Operating expenses (taxes, insurance, maintenance, management)
- Financing terms (down payment, interest rate, LTV)
- Net Operating Income (NOI) and cash flow projections
- Cap Rate and Cash-on-Cash return calculations
- For flips: purchase price + renovation costs vs. projected sale price
- Dual strategy display showing both Cash-on-Cash and Flip ROI simultaneously

### Strategy Selection
- **Rent Strategy**: Buy a property, find tenants, collect monthly income, manage maintenance. Success measured by Cash-on-Cash return and total deal return over the holding period. Rehab budget and timeline available before tenants move in.
- **Flip Strategy**: Buy a property, renovate it, sell for profit. Success depends on purchase price discipline, renovation budget accuracy, and market timing. Players choose a Rehab Finish Quality (Builder Grade to Luxury) that affects both costs and potential sale price. Flip profits are tied to rehab effort + diligence depth.

### Due Diligence System
Four types of due diligence, each revealing different property information:
- **Inspection**: Reveals structural, mechanical, and cosmetic issues
- **Appraisal**: Confirms or adjusts the property's market value
- **Comps Analysis**: Shows comparable sales data for pricing accuracy
- **Title Search**: Uncovers liens, easements, or title defects

More due diligence reduces risk and can earn rent premiums (1-3% for 2+ diligence types — better tenant screening, lease negotiation). Without comps, flip uncertainty range widens.

### Contractor & Renovation System
Players choose from Budget, Standard, and Premium contractor tiers via the Contractor Walkthrough Modal. The modal shows:
- Per-repair annual yield percentage and payback period
- Market condition banners (hot markets increase costs but also potential rent; soft markets offer cheaper labor but limited rent upside)
- Itemized repairs panel with approximate rent impact for rental strategy repairs
- Condition-aware AND property-type-aware upgrade recommendations (35+ upgrades organized by condition tier)

Renovation upgrades include:
- **Rough properties**: HVAC, windows, electrical panel, water heater, roof repair, security doors
- **Mid-range properties**: Paint, flooring, appliances, garage door, exterior paint, fencing, laundry hookup
- **Good properties**: Kitchen refresh, bathroom update, deck/patio, hardwood refinishing, closet systems
- **Luxury properties**: Spa bathroom, custom finishes, wine bar, outdoor kitchen, home theater, premium smart home, designer landscaping

Property-type-specific upgrades: HVAC/windows/roof (houses only), laundry hookup (condos/apartments), rooftop patio (urban units), balcony refresh (condos), separate utility meters (duplexes), exposed brick (lofts/townhouses), built-in storage (condos/apartments/lofts).

### Tenant Satisfaction System
Tenants have a satisfaction score (0-100, initialized 70-85):
- Unfixed issues lower satisfaction each month (severity-weighted: mild -1, moderate -2, severe -4, capped at -12/month)
- No issues: recovery +5/month
- Mood indicator: Happy (≥65), Concerned (≥30), Unhappy (<30) shown with tooltip
- Persistent unhappiness (below 30 for 3+ consecutive months AND active 4+ months) triggers departure risk (4% base + 3%/week over 3 unhappy, cap 22%)
- Turnover costs $500-$1,500 with 1 month vacancy

### Late Payment System
Each tenant is assigned a payment ethic on creation:
- Perfect (25%): 0% late chance
- Good (40%): 3% late chance, pays 85-92%
- Occasional (20%): 10% late chance, pays 85-92%
- Chronic (15%): 25% late chance, pays 65-85%
Late payment appears as "Late rent" debit in ledger. Tenant texts the player about being short. Property-managed rentals get deductions but no text messages.

### Lease Renewal System
Tenants have 6-month leases. At each renewal, rent adjusts based on:
- Market conditions (terrible -6% to excellent +5% with randomness)
- Tenant satisfaction (happy tenants accept increases, unhappy demand discounts)
- Unfixed property issues (suppress rent growth)
- Cosmetic upgrades (small bonus)
- Change capped at ±8% per renewal, hard floor/ceiling at 70-135% of activation rent
- Rent is stable between renewals — market shifts no longer adjust rent mid-lease

### Progressive Expense Escalation
Unfixed rental issues get worse over time:
- Months 1-3: Normal
- Months 4-6: Building (1.3x cost/probability)
- Months 7-9: Serious (1.6x)
- Months 10-12: Critical (2.0x)
- Months 13+: Severe (2.5x)
Multiple unfixed issues compound via severity factor.

### Market-Driven Mechanics
Market conditions influence:
- Rent at lease renewal time (not mid-lease)
- Renovation costs and potential rent impact
- Property sale prices (6 factors: time held, diligence count, unfixed issues, tenant satisfaction, cosmetic upgrades, market variance)
- Quick-flip penalty: selling within 2 months caps at 95% of purchase price

### Flip Rebalancing
- No-rehab flips cap below purchase price (wholesale deals)
- Low rehab (<25%) caps gains at 8%
- Spread capture uses completionFactor^0.7 curve
- Rare 3% windfall for diligent rehabbers

### Rental Sale Pricing (Multi-Factor)
When selling a rental property, 6 factors determine price:
1. Time held (0.4%/month appreciation, cap 10%)
2. Diligence count (-2% for none up to +7% for all 4)
3. Unfixed/undiscovered issue penalty (2-2.5% each)
4. Tenant satisfaction bonus (+2% happy, -3% very unhappy)
5. Cosmetic upgrade boost
6. Market variance
Floor at 60% of purchase price.

### Execution Phase
After committing to a deal, players experience a month-by-month timeline with:
- Maintenance events (appliance failures, plumbing leaks, HVAC issues, storm damage)
- Tenant satisfaction tracking and potential turnover
- Market condition shifts affecting rent and property values
- Renovation opportunities with contractor options
- Progressive expense escalation for unfixed issues
- Surprise events and curveballs
- Overtime mode for extended gameplay

### Post-Deal Analysis
Every completed deal includes a detailed postmortem:
- Side-by-side comparison of pro forma projections vs. actual outcomes
- Letter grades (A+ through F) for prediction accuracy
- Explanatory reasons for gaps between projections and reality
- Shareable deal summary card
- Rental Reality Reveal screen with phased animation and confetti for good grades

## Free Interactive Tools

### Flip or Rent Strategy Analyzer
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/tools/flip-or-rent

An interactive calculator that compares flipping vs. renting the same property. Users input purchase price, estimated rent, renovation costs, and market assumptions. The tool calculates ROI, cash flow, and total returns for both strategies at 1, 3, and 5-year horizons.

### Deal Scorecard
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/tools/deal-scorecard

Tests any investment property against 7 established rules of thumb simultaneously:
- 1% Rule (monthly rent ≥ 1% of purchase price)
- 2% Rule (aggressive cash flow threshold)
- 50% Rule (operating expenses ≈ 50% of gross income)
- 70% Rule (maximum purchase price for flips)
- Cap Rate analysis (NOI / property value)
- Gross Rent Multiplier (price / annual rent)
- Cash-on-Cash Return (annual cash flow / total cash invested)

Returns an instant letter grade (A through F) with detailed breakdown.

## Educational Articles (Learning Center)

### What Is a Pro Forma in Real Estate?
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/what-is-a-pro-forma
Difficulty: Beginner | Read time: 5 min
Covers the anatomy of a pro forma, why assumptions matter, rental vs. flip pro formas, and break-even occupancy rates. The pro forma is called "your deal's truth serum" — it strips away emotional appeal and reveals whether a property actually makes money.

### Cap Rates & Cash-on-Cash Returns: The Real Story
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/cap-rates-cash-on-cash
Difficulty: Beginner | Read time: 6 min
Explains two metrics that tell completely different things about the same deal. Cap rate ignores financing (NOI / Property Value). Cash-on-Cash measures what YOUR money earns. Covers the cap rate spectrum (3-4% premium areas to 11%+ distressed), the inverse dance of prices and cap rates, and yield on cost for value-add investors.

### Flip vs. Rent: The Strategy Decision That Changes Everything
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/flip-vs-rent
Difficulty: Beginner | Read time: 7 min
Compares the two fundamental real estate strategies. Flipping = active income (like a job). Renting = passive income (like a business). Covers holding costs that eat flip profits, the rental cash flow flywheel, and market condition timing for each strategy.

### Due Diligence: The $500 That Saves You $50,000
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/due-diligence
Difficulty: Beginner | Read time: 6 min
The four pillars of due diligence: inspection, appraisal, comps analysis, and title search. Each reveals different risks. Covers common inspection red flags ($500 inspection vs. $50,000 surprise), and why skipping any step is gambling.

### LTV & Financing: The Double-Edged Sword of Leverage
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/ltv-financing
Difficulty: Intermediate | Read time: 6 min
Loan-to-Value ratio fundamentals, how down payments create leverage, the double-edged sword of high LTV (amplifies both gains and losses), and why lenders care about LTV thresholds (80%, 75%, 70%).

### Reading Market Conditions Like a Pro
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/market-conditions
Difficulty: Intermediate | Read time: 6 min
How market cycles (terrible through excellent) affect every part of a deal: purchase prices, rents, renovation costs, days on market, and exit strategy viability. The four seasons of real estate and what each means for investors.

### Rehab Budgets: Where Deals Go to Die (or Thrive)
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/rehab-budgets
Difficulty: Intermediate | Read time: 6 min
How to plan renovations that actually add value. Covers common renovation cost ranges, contractor tier selection (Budget/Standard/Premium), the no-rehab flip strategy, and cash vs. finance decisions for renovation funding.

### The 5 Mistakes That Bankrupt New Investors
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/common-mistakes
Difficulty: Beginner | Read time: 7 min
Fantasy rent numbers, invisible expenses, the leverage trap, speed over safety, and running without cash reserves. Every one looks reasonable until it costs you everything.

### The 1% Rule and Other Quick Screening Filters
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/one-percent-rule
Difficulty: Intermediate | Read time: 5 min
How to evaluate 50 properties in an hour. The 1% Rule, 50% Rule, 70% Rule for flips, and when these rules of thumb fail. Building a personal filter stack to eliminate 90% of listings quickly.

### How to Survive (and Profit From) a Market Crash
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/survive-market-crash
Difficulty: Advanced | Read time: 7 min
The bankruptcy cascade, crash-proof portfolio structure, and how to profit during panic. Recession indicators and why direction matters more than timing precision.

### The Hidden Costs Nobody Tells You About
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/hidden-costs
Difficulty: Intermediate | Read time: 6 min
14 expenses that don't show up in the listing: maintenance, CapEx, property management, vacancy loss, closing costs, legal/accounting, pest control, landscaping, holding costs for flippers, and the self-management illusion. Also covers tax implications (rental depreciation vs. flip ordinary income).

### Building a Real Estate Portfolio: From One Property to Ten
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/portfolio-strategy
Difficulty: Advanced | Read time: 8 min
The compounding cycle (Acquire → Improve → Refinance → Repeat), diversification across property types and locations, the cash flow tipping point (3-4 stabilized rentals), and capital recycling.

### Tenant Management: The Human Side of Real Estate
URL: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/learn/tenant-management
Difficulty: Intermediate | Read time: 6 min
Screening (a bad tenant costs 10x more than vacancy), communication playbook, maintenance balance, and when to raise rent (keep good tenants at slightly below-market, turnover costs 1-2 months vacancy plus $500-2,000).

## Technical Details

- Platform: Web browser (desktop and mobile responsive)
- Mobile app: iOS (React Native with Expo, WebView wrapper)
- Cost: Free to play, no signup required
- Optional: In-game boosts available for purchase (never required)
- Technology: React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL
- RSS Feed: https://dealbreaksimulator.com/feed.xml
